analyst: redundancy-analyzer skill (scope=cross-app). Companion nil report to redundancy-matrix.json.
determination: NO VARIANCE COMPUTABLE — nil report, for two independent reasons, either of which alone would be sufficient.

reasons.detail: Regulatory variance analysis applies only to applications whose business rules trace to a regulation. The upstream business-logic-extraction pass evaluated this wave's sole application against the governing faa profile's regulatory_sources (14 CFR Part 47 aircraft registration, Part 61 pilot certification, Part 63 other flight crewmembers, Part 67 medical standards, Part 183 representatives of the Administrator) and recorded match_result 'No match on any entry': the application is a standalone student-academic-records desktop tool with no airman, certificate, rating, medical, endorsement, aircraft, registration, designee or examiner entity anywhere in its single 10-column table or its 461 lines of hand-written code. All 60 extracted rules are business conventions, defects or implementation artifacts, and regulatory_traceability is omitted from every one of them rather than populated with a fabricated citation.

Implementation variance is a comparison of how two or more applications implement the same regulation section. The wave roster declared in the dispatch context contains exactly one application (c70846ac-0948-4953-990c-c68a2be292d9), so even for a regulation that WERE implemented here there would be no second implementation to compare it against and no canonical-versus-divergent determination to make.

notes: A nil report is emitted rather than no file at all, so that a reader of this wave's evidence body can tell that regulatory variance was assessed and found undefined, rather than skipped.

Carried forward, NOT adopted as a finding of this skill: the governing profile for this dispatch is 'faa' and every input artifact agrees faa is authoritative, so there is no profile-declaration conflict. What the catalog, structural-analysis, business-logic and ux-accessibility passes each independently flag is that this application's domain has no plausible aviation, NAS or FAA relevance — a profile-ASSIGNMENT question for the engagement owner, not a redundancy or variance question. It is recorded here because it is the reason the regulatory match set is empty.

The faa profile's compliance.yaml Part 47 applicable_systems list is self-described by the upstream pass as carrying an unresolved TODO(human) marker, so that list is unconfirmed. This does not change the determination: the application has no aviation entity of any kind, so no plausible completion of that list would produce a match.

If a later wave introduces a second application that implements any of the faa profile's regulatory sources, regulatory variance becomes computable for that wave and must be rescored. Nothing in this nil report forecloses that.
